Type argument violates upper bound of T
Anonymous override requires an exact inherited method signature
Anonymous supertype arguments cannot be projected
Anonymous override result differs from inherited method
Anonymous generic Unit results require unsupported boxed Unit overrides

limitations: Concrete generic and nongeneric class and interface bases with constructor substitution, override specialization, erased bridges and JVM generic superclass/interface signatures. Own members must be override functions; anonymous properties, generic methods and covariant bridges remain diagnosed. Superclass default/reordered arguments and conflicting inherited defaults are outside this evidence.

Anonymous supertype arguments referencing enclosing type parameters are explicitly unsupported. Generated anonymous classes retain the existing lack of EnclosingMethod and anonymous Kotlin metadata. Reflection equivalence and generic anonymous identity in exported APIs are not claimed.
Java callers compile once against official Kotlin output, then execute unchanged with verification against both providers.
